topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and loss of growth control
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture, states its aims, and introduces the hallmarks framework before the substantive material begins.

topics.label: Growth-control signaling through Wnt, Ras–MAPK, PI3K–AKT, and TGF-beta
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how extracellular signals regulate proliferation and survival and how mutations in the signaling pathways disrupt that regulation.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in hematological and intestinal cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how impaired differentiation appears in blood cancers and in intestinal epithelium after APC loss.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis through p53 and BAX–BCL2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how changes in p53 and the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins allow cancer cells to evade cell death.

topics.label: Telomere limits, senescence, and p53-mediated growth safeguards
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening and cellular stress trigger growth-limiting responses, how TERT can help cancer cells bypass telomere limits, and recap mutation-driven growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism and metabolic reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe cancer-associated glycolysis and tissue-specific metabolic changes, including how altered metabolites can affect the epigenome.

topics.label: The angiogenic switch in tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors recruit blood vessels to obtain the oxygen and nutrients needed for continued growth.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination, survival, and secondary-site growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow cancer cells through dissemination and colonization, explaining metastatic inefficiency, site compatibility, and the genomic features observed in metastases.

topics.label: Lecture summary and closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic recaps the lecture’s central point about diverse routes to shared cancer hallmarks and closes with questions and practical-session information.
